principles: Gate evidence must be atomically durable before a writer reports success.
Causal exact deltas are admissible; path-shaped or text-shaped dirt is not.
Failure rolls back framework-owned bytes without modifying competing user data.
drivers: Prevent long validations from being invalidated by quorum-owned residue.
Preserve independent reviewer/host submission semantics without owner self-signing.
Reuse proven short exact metadata transaction primitives instead of inventing a broad exception.

options.name: A: Exact quorum-local metadata transaction
pros: Binds admission to the current invocation
Can commit all six verdicts atomically
cons: Requires a focused transaction wrapper and failure tests

options.name: B: Teach validate to accept dirty host verdict rows
cons: Launders pre-existing or forged verdict-shaped dirt
Moves responsibility to the wrong writer

options.name: C: Host manually commits after quorum_submit
cons: Relies on memory and shell discipline
Already caused a nine-minute wasted run
Cannot guarantee atomic rollback or prevent partial quorum

rationale: Only option A preserves the verifier fail-closed boundary while making quorum_submit responsible for the exact L4 evidence it emits. It eliminates the observed residue without granting a path-based trust exception.

preMortem.scenario: The transaction commits pre-existing or forged process-event rows together with the quorum batch.
preMortem.trigger: process-events.jsonl is dirty before quorum_submit or changes outside the captured exact suffix.
preMortem.consequence: Untrusted evidence can enter a trusted commit and influence DONE assurance.
preMortem.mitigation: Require a clean bounded entry state, capture exact pre-bytes/HEAD, compare the post suffix structurally and fail closed without staging on mismatch.

preMortem.scenario: A hook or commit failure leaves three of six verdicts or a dirty file behind.
preMortem.trigger: Git hook rejects the commit or persistence throws after some append operations.
preMortem.consequence: A partial quorum may be consumed or the next validation is poisoned.
preMortem.mitigation: Capture before mutation, emit in memory/bounded file transaction, rollback exact bytes and index on any failure, then assert no current-material verdict remains.

preMortem.scenario: A concurrent writer appends a legitimate process event while quorum_submit is closing.
preMortem.trigger: HEAD or process-events bytes move between emission and commit.
preMortem.consequence: Quorum may overwrite, absorb or delete another writer’s evidence.
preMortem.mitigation: CAS recheck both HEAD and exact content; abort and preserve competing bytes with a classified retryable infra failure.

preMortem.scenario: Duplicate retry creates a second six-row quorum after the first commit succeeded.
preMortem.trigger: Caller retries after losing terminal output.
preMortem.consequence: Duplicate runIds pollute assurance and audit history.
preMortem.mitigation: Retain same-material duplicate detection before emission and add an idempotent retry regression.
